$comment: Species charters. A species is a design space, not a keyword: nothing is printed on every card of a species. Each charter names a centre of gravity (the effects this species should get a disproportionate share of), a hole (what it is genuinely bad at, which is what actually creates identity), and a signature (an effect only this species does). scripts/identity.mjs measures the card set against this file and fails when two species become indistinguishable or a signature goes unused. Owl is the tenth species (Night Shift, v0.7.0). Studies are the other, horizontal axis: species is what a card IS, study is what it DOES, and a deck is one or two of each.

Rabbit.blurb: Rabbits arrive in crowds. One Rabbit is nothing much; six Rabbits are a town.
Rabbit.hole: Low output per animal, and a cheap curve that runs out of ladder early in a bidding war.
Rabbit.signatureText: Recruiting further Characters out of hand, especially other Rabbits.

Mouse.blurb: Mice do the paperwork. They make the Events everyone else cannot afford to play.
Mouse.hole: Weak shifts and almost no presence in the Capital City.
Mouse.signatureText: Replaying Events and discounting their requirements.

Badger.blurb: Badgers dig in. What knocks a town over leaves a Badger standing.
Badger.hole: Slow, and very little card flow — a Badger town sees fewer cards than anyone's.
Badger.signatureText: Shrugging off an on-reveal Market card that would hit both towns.

Hedgehog.blurb: Hedgehogs are impossible to move and impossible to bother.
Hedgehog.hole: No reach whatsoever: a Hedgehog deck cannot touch the rival's town at all.
Hedgehog.signatureText: Making a Character untargetable, or immune to Unemployment.

Raccoon.blurb: Raccoons work the bins. One town's discard is a Raccoon's hand.
Raccoon.hole: Fragile and poor at shifts; a Raccoon rarely out-earns anyone.
Raccoon.signatureText: Taking a card out of the shared City Dump — nobody else touches it.

Fox.blurb: Foxes read the room. They know what is coming and what it is worth.
Fox.hole: Poor raw economy — Foxes never win by out-earning you.
Fox.signatureText: Changing a bid, a pledge or an auction's terms after it has opened.

Otter.blurb: Otters keep everything moving. Work slides from paw to paw and nothing sits still.
Otter.hole: No protection and no disruption: Otters cannot stop anything, only outpace it.
Otter.signatureText: Moving a shift or a readiness from one Character to another.

Squirrel.blurb: Squirrels put things by. A Squirrel town is poor all game and rich exactly once.
Squirrel.hole: Slow starts — everything a Squirrel does pays later than everyone else's.
Squirrel.signatureText: Caching Supply on a card, safe from shared shocks, to be spent later.

Cat.blurb: Cats do as they please, which is usually the right thing at the wrong moment.
Cat.hole: Cats do not co-operate: they are the worst species for anything counting friends or species.
Cat.signatureText: Ignoring an orientation rule — acting when a Character should not be able to.

Owl.blurb: Owls are awake when the rest of the town is asleep. They see what is coming, and they have everybody up and working before dawn.
Owl.hole: Owls earn almost nothing on their own and want no part of a bidding war: an Owl town is wise, awake and poor, and an Owl would sooner read the pledge ladder than climb it.
Owl.signatureText: The wake-up call: turning a Character one step toward upright outside the Ready phase, never one that is mid-shift.
